title: Spatial strategies
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:50Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches map and GIS tools for showing and analysing where things are, while the new point is about planning where things should go, such as wildlife corridors and city plans, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Spatial strategies
card: A spatial strategy is a plan for where things should go in a place. It uses the layout of land, buildings and transport to reduce harm to the environment.
a strip of bush or vegetation that links separate patches of habitat, so animals can move between them to find food and mates.
a plan that places homes, jobs, shops and public transport close together, so people can make shorter trips and use less energy.
These strategies work by changing where things are, not only by banning actions.
draft.remember: Spatial strategies reduce harm by planning where things go.

a.q: What is the main purpose of a wildlife corridor between two patches of bush?
opts: To let animals move between the habitat patches
To keep animals inside one patch of bush
To make a path for tourists to follow
To stop new trees from growing in the strip
a.why: A corridor links habitats, so animals can travel to find food and mates. Keeping animals in one patch is the opposite of what it does, because the patches would stay cut off.
a.clue: Think about what happens to animals in isolated patches.

b.q: A council plans a new suburb with shops, jobs and a train station within walking distance of homes. How does this plan help the environment?
opts: Shorter trips mean less car travel and energy use
It stops people from owning any cars at all
It makes the suburb larger so the bush is cleared
It moves jobs far away so homes stay quiet
b.why: Placing things close together shortens trips, so people drive less and use less energy. The plan does not ban cars. It changes where things are.
b.clue: Look at the distance between homes and daily needs.

a.best: To let animals move between the habitat patches

b.best: Shorter trips mean less car travel and energy use
